hooks.text: A 50-foot steel tank in Boston was leaking 2,300,000 gallons.
Why did a massive steel tank in Boston suddenly turn brown?
2,300,000 gallons of molasses were held by a single leaking tank.

title: Why Was the Boston Molasses Tank Painted Brown? ⚠️
description: In 1919, a massive molasses tank in Boston's North End exploded, sending a deadly wave through the streets. The owners had ignored the leaks, choosing to hide them with paint instead.

beats.text: A 50-foot steel tank in Boston was leaking 2,300,000 gallons.
beats.visual: photograph of the Purity Distilling Company molasses tank in Boston, 1919

beats.text: In 1919, the owners ignored obvious structural cracks to save money.
beats.visual: photograph of United States Industrial Alcohol Company document or logo

beats.text: On a warm winter day, the structure ruptured in the North End.
beats.visual: photograph of the wreckage immediately after the Boston Molasses Flood, 1919

beats.text: A 35 mile per hour wave killed at least 21 people.
beats.visual: photograph of damaged buildings and debris in the North End, 1919

beats.text: To hide the leaks, the company had simply painted it brown.
beats.visual: close up photograph of the molasses tank steel plates showing leakage stains, 1919

beats.text: No one was ever charged for the 50-foot steel tank leaking.
beats.visual: photograph of rescue workers and cleanup crews in the ruins, 1919
